title: Conservative ingress pacing, small-payload routing, and streaming proxy watermark tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: recent customer incidents showed increased streaming jitter and intermittent fncall handshake timeouts under bursty ingress from low-latency mobile clients. This PR applies a conservative, ingress-side pacing layer and a small-payload fast-path in the router to reduce head-of-line effects, while tuning streaming proxy watermarks to balance latency vs backpressure. The change also tightens the fncall handshake timeout to fail fast on malformed tool calls and improves the OpenAI-compat layer to provide clearer 413 guidance. Changes are deliberately conservative to avoid behavior surprises for high-throughput backends. Checklist: * add token-bucket ingress pacing with configurable defaults; * introduce "small_payload_fastlane" router rule (payloads < 2KB) to prefer low-latency worker pools; * reduce streaming proxy high-watermark from 256KB to 64KB and lower low-watermark to 16KB; * add fncall handshake 500ms conservative timeout and clearer error mapping for compatibility layer; * add integration tests for paced ingress + fncall and structured output streaming; * update API docs and console route settings UI; * observe metrics in staging for 48h before rolling to prod. Impact: this will change routing decisions for small requests and may slightly increase tail latency for large-batch workloads if operators choose very low pacing buckets. Default values are set to be non-breaking for most customers and can be tuned per-tenant. Related: ENG-4321 (streaming stability initiative), ENG-4390 (gateway QoS), SUP-712 (customer incident), and an internal runbook was created.

release_notes: Gateway: introduce conservative ingress pacing to reduce streaming jitter; Router: add small-payload fastlane to favor low-latency workers for requests < 2KB; Proxy: tune streaming buffer watermarks (high=64KB, low=16KB) to enforce earlier backpressure; Fncall: add 500ms handshake deadline to fail fast on malformed calls; OpenAI compatibility: clearer 413 payload-too-large guidance. Rollout: staged in staging for 48h with new observability metrics; defaults are conservative and per-tenant tunables are provided.
rationale: Bursty low-latency clients were causing head-of-line blocking at the gateway which manifested as streaming jitter and intermittent fncall handshake timeouts. Conservative ingress pacing smooths bursts without changing client API. Small-payload fastlane reduces latency for conversational-style requests common in assistant features. Watermark tuning reduces the proxy's internal buffering so backpressure signals reach upstream sooner and prevent large memory accumulation.
impact_notes: Behavioral changes: small requests (<2KB) may be routed to different worker pools; operators can opt-out per-route. Lower proxy watermarks may surface backpressure to clients earlier (you may see more 429s for large bursts until downstream autoscaling adjusts). Fncall handshake deadline may cause clients with slow network to receive faster failures — increase per-route timeout if needed.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket logic and stream buffer boundaries; integration tests simulating bursty ingress and fncall handshakes; end-to-end smoke in staging for 48h with metrics collection (gateway.ingress.paced_requests, proxy.buffer.high_watermark_events, fncall.handshake.timeouts). Manual verification of console route toggle and API docs. Observe error budget and latency SLOs during rollout.
notes: Operator guidance added to docs/api/limits.md and console UI; recommend enabling small_payload_fastlane only after reviewing traffic profile. If you rely on strict ordering across payload sizes, set per-route 'preserve_order' to true (note: may reduce throughput).
